intro: Buddhists care a lot about a calm mind and a kind heart. They practice meditation. They try to be kind to every living thing.
In this unit you will learn what meditation is and where Buddhists do it. You will hear the story of a swan. You will be able to tell what metta and the five precepts are.
bigQuestion: How do Buddhists practice calm and kindness?

timeline.t: A family takes off their shoes and enters a temple.
A nun rings a small bell, and the room goes quiet.
People sit still and pay attention; this is meditation.
Buddhists say the mind settles like still water.
Young Siddhartha saves a swan with an arrow in its wing.
The wise men say a life belongs to the one who saves it.
Buddhists wish loving-kindness, metta, for all beings.
Many Buddhists make five promises about how to live.

words.d: a practice of sitting still and paying close attention
a building where people gather to practice their religion
a man who gives his life to religious practice
a woman who gives her life to religious practice
to tell what something is like
loving-kindness; wishing all beings to be happy and safe
a promise or rule about how to live
anything that is alive, like people, animals and bugs

test.why: Buddhists say it helps the mind grow calm and clear.

test.q: What do we do with meditation in school?
test.why: In class we describe the practice; families choose what they do.

test.q: What might start quiet time at a temple?
test.why: Many temples use a bell to start and end quiet time.

test.q: In the jar picture, what happens when the water is still?
test.why: The sand settles and the water clears.
In the story Siddhartha gently cared for the swan.
Metta means loving-kindness toward all beings.

test.q: How many precepts do many Buddhists take?
test.why: Many Buddhists take the five precepts.

test.q: Which is one of the five precepts?
choices: do not take what is not given
test.why: Not taking what is not given is the second precept.

test.q: Which shows kindness to a living thing?
test.why: Buddhists try not to hurt living things, even small bugs.

write.prompt: Tell about one way Buddhists practice calm or kindness. Use the swan story, metta, or the five precepts. Tell what Buddhists say it helps.
tips: Name the story or the word you use.
Use one unit word, like metta or precept.

title: Calm and Kindness

chapters.title: Breathing and Being Still
chapters.bigQuestion: What is meditation, and why do Buddhists practice it?

story.title: The Little Bell
story.kicker: A small bell rings, and a whole room goes quiet.
paragraphs: Mia and her grandma visit a Buddhist temple on Sunday. They take off their shoes at the door. Inside, the room smells like flowers. People sit on round cushions.
At the front, a nun in a brown robe holds a small bell. She taps it once. Ding. The sound is soft and long. The whole room goes quiet.
Mia's grandma sits very still. Her hands rest in her lap. Her eyes are almost closed. Mia watches. Nobody talks. She can hear a bird outside.
Later Mia asks, "What were you doing, Grandma?" Grandma smiles. "I was meditating. It helps my mind feel calm and clear."
story.think: What did Mia notice in the quiet room?

lessons.title: Sitting Still and Paying Attention
lessons.mainIdea: Meditation is a practice of sitting still and paying attention.
reading: Buddhists practice meditation. They often sit still. They pay close attention, often to their breathing.
Buddhists say meditation helps the mind grow calm and clear. Some meditate for a few minutes. Some meditate for a long time.

words.d: a practice of sitting still and paying close attention

look.title: A Quiet Room
look.text: Look at a room with soft light. People sit on cushions in rows. Their backs are straight. Their hands rest in their laps. No one is talking.
look.prompt: What words would you use to tell about this room?

check.q: What is meditation?
check.why: Meditation is a practice of sitting still and paying close attention.

check.q: What do Buddhists often pay attention to?
check.why: Buddhists often pay attention to their breathing when they meditate.

check.q: What do Buddhists say meditation helps?
choices: the mind grow calm and clear
check.why: Buddhists say it helps the mind grow calm and clear.

lessons.title: Learning About, Not Doing
lessons.mainIdea: In class we learn about meditation; we tell about it, not do it.
reading: In school we learn about many things people do. We learn how farmers plant. We learn how Buddhists meditate.
Learning about something is not the same as doing it. We describe what Buddhists do. Families can choose what they practice at home.

words.d: to tell what something is like

look.title: Learning About Jobs
look.text: Your class reads a book about firefighters. You learn about their hats and trucks. You do not put out a fire. You learn about the job.
look.prompt: How is learning about meditation like learning about firefighters?

check.q: What do we do in class?
check.why: In class we describe the practice; we learn about it.

check.q: What does describe mean?
check.why: To describe is to tell what something is like.

check.q: Who chooses what a family practices?
check.why: Families choose what they practice at home.

lessons.title: Monks, Nuns and Families
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhist monks, nuns and families meditate at temples and at home.
reading: Buddhist monks and nuns live a simple life. They wear robes. They often meditate every day, sometimes in the morning and evening.
Many Buddhist families meditate too. Some go to a temple. Some sit at home near a small altar with a Buddha image and flowers.

words.d: a man who gives his life to religious practice
a woman who gives her life to religious practice

look.title: A Home Altar
look.text: Look at a small shelf in a living room. On it is a calm Buddha statue. Next to it are fresh flowers, a candle and a bowl of oranges.
look.prompt: Why might a family keep flowers and fruit by the statue?

check.q: Who wears robes and meditates every day?
check.why: Buddhist monks and nuns often meditate every day.

check.q: What is a nun?
choices: a woman who gives her life to religious practice
check.why: A nun is a woman who gives her life to religious practice.

check.q: Where might a family meditate?
choices: at a temple or at home
check.why: Many families meditate at a temple or near a home altar.

lessons.title: The Temple Bell
lessons.mainIdea: Temples often use a bell to begin and end quiet time.
reading: Many Buddhist temples use a bell. A soft ring can mean quiet time is starting. Another ring can mean it is over.
Some temples have big bells that ring deep and slow. Some use small bowls that sing when tapped.

words.d: a building where people gather to practice their religion

look.title: Buddhists in the World
look.cite: Pew Research Center, The Global Religious Landscape (2012), rounded

check.q: What can a soft bell mean at a temple?
check.why: Many temples ring a bell to start and end quiet time.

check.q: What is a temple?
choices: a building where people practice their religion
check.why: A temple is a building where people gather to practice their religion.

check.q: About how many Buddhists are in the world?
check.why: Common estimates say about 500 million Buddhists live in the world.

lessons.title: Calm and Clear
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhists compare a calm mind to still, clear water.
reading: Buddhist teachers sometimes use a picture. Muddy water that is shaken stays cloudy. When it sits still, the mud settles. The water gets clear.
Buddhists say the mind is like that water. They say meditation helps it settle and grow clear.

words.d: easy to see through

look.title: The Jar of Water
look.text: Look at a jar of water with sand in it. Shake it, and the water is cloudy. Set it down. Wait. The sand sinks slowly. Now you can see through the water.
look.prompt: What happens to the water when it sits still?

check.q: What happens when the jar sits still?
check.why: When the jar is still, the sand sinks and the water clears.

check.q: What do Buddhists compare the mind to?
check.why: Buddhist teachers compare the mind to water that can settle.

check.q: What does clear mean?
check.why: Clear means easy to see through.

lessons.title: Quiet Is for Everyone
lessons.mainIdea: Many people, Buddhist or not, find quiet time helpful.
reading: Many people who are not Buddhist also like quiet time. Some sit in a park. Some rest in a calm corner.
Everyone finds calm in different ways. Some like to draw. Some like to hug a pet. What helps you feel calm?

words.d: with little or no sound

look.title: A Calm Corner
look.text: Look at a corner of a classroom. There is a soft rug and a pillow. A basket holds books and a squishy ball. A child sits there and feels calm.
look.prompt: What would you put in a calm corner?

check.q: Do only Buddhists like quiet time?
check.why: Many people, Buddhist or not, find quiet time helpful.

check.q: Which is one way to feel calm?
check.why: People find calm in many ways, like drawing.

check.q: What does quiet mean?
check.why: Quiet means with little or no sound.

review.why: Buddhists describe meditation as sitting still and paying attention.

review.q: What did the bell do in Mia's temple?
review.why: The nun rang the bell and the room went quiet.
Monks and nuns often meditate every day.

review.q: What do we do with meditation in class?
review.why: In class we describe what Buddhists do.

review.q: What does the jar of muddy water show?
choices: how Buddhists say the mind settles
review.why: Buddhists compare a calm mind to water that settles.

review.q: What might be on a home altar?
review.why: Many home altars have a Buddha image, flowers, a candle or fruit.

chapters.title: Kind to Every Living Thing
chapters.bigQuestion: What do Buddhists teach about being kind to every living thing?

story.title: The Swan and the Two Cousins
story.kicker: A swan falls from the sky, and two cousins both run to it.
paragraphs: Buddhists tell this story about young Siddhartha. One day he was in the garden. A white swan fell from the sky. An arrow was stuck in its wing.
Siddhartha ran to the swan. He gently pulled out the arrow. He held the bird close to keep it warm. The swan was scared but alive.
Then his cousin Devadatta ran up. "That is my swan!" he said. "I shot it down." Siddhartha held on. "I saved it," he said. "It should stay with me."
The two boys went to the wise men of the court. The wise men thought hard. They said, "A life belongs to the one who saves it, not the one who hurts it."
story.think: Do you agree with the wise men? Why?

lessons.title: Saving the Swan
lessons.mainIdea: In the story, young Siddhartha helped a hurt swan.
reading: Buddhists tell that Siddhartha found a swan with an arrow in its wing. He took the arrow out gently. He cared for the bird.
The story shows that even as a boy, Siddhartha was kind. He wanted to help living things, not hurt them.

words.d: in a soft and careful way

look.title: Holding the Swan
look.text: Look at a boy kneeling in the grass. He holds a white swan in his arms. He talks softly to it. A small arrow lies on the ground beside him.
look.prompt: How do you know the boy cares about the swan?

check.q: What was wrong with the swan?
choices: an arrow was in its wing
check.why: The story says an arrow was stuck in its wing.

check.q: What did Siddhartha do?
check.why: He gently pulled out the arrow and cared for the bird.

check.q: What does gently mean?
choices: in a soft and careful way
check.why: Gently means in a soft and careful way.

lessons.title: Who Should Keep It?
lessons.mainIdea: The wise men said a life belongs to the one who saves it.
reading: Devadatta said the swan was his because he shot it. Siddhartha said it should stay with him because he saved it.
The wise men decided. The one who saves a life should keep it. The one who hurts it should not.

words.d: the child of your aunt or uncle

look.title: Two Claims
look.text: Devadatta says, "I shot it, so it is mine." Siddhartha says, "I saved it, so it should stay with me." The wise men must choose.
look.prompt: What reason did the wise men give?

check.q: Who shot the swan?
check.why: In the story, Devadatta shot the swan.

check.q: What did the wise men decide?
choices: the one who shoots it keeps it
the one who saves it keeps it
check.why: They said a life belongs to the one who saves it.

check.q: What is a cousin?
choices: the child of your aunt or uncle
check.why: A cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle.

lessons.title: Metta for All Beings
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhists teach metta, loving-kindness toward all beings.
reading: Buddhists have a word, metta. It means loving-kindness. It is a warm wish that everyone be happy and safe.
An old Buddhist text says to wish well for all beings, big and small, near and far. Buddhists say this wish is like a mother caring for her child.

words.d: loving-kindness; wishing all beings to be happy and safe

look.title: A Wish for All
look.text: May all beings, big or small, near or far, be happy and safe. Care for them the way a mother cares for her only child.
look.cite: Karaniya Metta Sutta, Sutta Nipata 1.8, retold in simple words

check.q: What does metta mean?
check.why: Metta is a Pali word meaning loving-kindness.

check.q: Who is metta for?
check.why: The Metta Sutta wishes well for all beings, big and small.

check.q: What picture does the text use?
choices: a mother caring for her child
check.why: The Karaniya Metta Sutta compares metta to a mother's care.

lessons.title: Do Not Hurt Living Things
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhists try not to hurt living things, big or small.
reading: Many Buddhists try not to hurt living things. Some carry a bug outside instead of squashing it. Many choose not to eat meat.
Buddhists say every living thing wants to be safe, just like us. So they try to be gentle with all of them.

words.d: anything that is alive, like people, animals and bugs

look.title: A Spider in the Kitchen
look.text: Look at a spider on the kitchen wall. A boy gets a cup and a card. He slides the spider into the cup. He carries it outside and lets it go in the grass.
look.prompt: Why did the boy carry the spider outside?

check.q: What might a Buddhist do with a bug in the house?
check.why: Many Buddhists try not to hurt living things, even small ones.

check.q: Which is a living thing?
check.why: A bug is alive. Rocks and chairs are not.

check.q: Why do Buddhists try not to hurt animals?
choices: every living thing wants to be safe
check.why: Buddhists say all living things want to be safe.

lessons.title: Promises Buddhists Make
lessons.mainIdea: Many Buddhists make five promises about how to live.
reading: Many Buddhists make five promises. They are called the five precepts. They try their best to keep them.
Told simply, they are: do not hurt living things, do not take what is not given, be faithful in families, tell the truth, and keep your mind clear.

words.d: a promise or rule about how to live
saying you will do something and meaning it

look.title: The Five Promises
rows: do not take what is not given
look.cite: The five precepts (pancasila), as recited by Buddhist laypeople, told simply

check.q: How many precepts do many Buddhists take?
check.why: Many Buddhists take five precepts.

check.q: Which is one of the five promises?
check.why: Telling the truth is one of the five precepts.

check.q: What is a precept?
choices: a promise about how to live
check.why: A precept is a promise or rule about how to live.

lessons.title: Sharing and Saying Sorry
lessons.mainIdea: Sharing and saying sorry are kind acts in any classroom.
reading: Buddhists teach giving and kindness. In class, kindness can look like sharing crayons. It can look like taking turns.
Sometimes we make a mistake. Saying sorry helps fix it. Then we can try again. Everyone is learning.

words.d: a word we say to show we wish we had not hurt someone

look.title: The Crayon Box
look.text: Look at two friends at a table. There is one box of crayons. One friend takes the red one. The other friend wants red too. They decide to take turns.
look.prompt: How did the friends solve their problem kindly?

check.q: Which is a kind act in class?
check.why: Sharing is a kind act, like the giving Buddhists teach.

check.q: What can you do after a mistake?
check.why: Saying sorry helps fix a mistake, and then you can try again.

check.q: What does taking turns show?
check.why: Taking turns is a kind way to share.

review.why: In the story, young Siddhartha saved the swan.

review.q: What did the wise men say?
choices: a life belongs to the one who saves it
review.why: They said the one who saves a life should keep it.
Metta means loving-kindness for all beings.

review.q: What is the first of the five precepts?
review.why: The first precept is not to hurt living things.
Devadatta was Siddhartha's cousin in the story.

review.q: Why do many Buddhists carry bugs outside?
review.why: Many Buddhists try not to harm any living thing.
